Guidance

Ebola and Marburg haemorrhagic fevers: outbreaks and case locations

Information about incidents and outbreaks of Ebola and Marburg, both viral haemorrhagic fevers (VHF).

From:
UK Health Security Agency
Published:
23 March 2014
Last updated:
27 August 2026 — See all updates

Contents

  1. Current incidents and outbreaks
  2. Previous incidents and outbreaks: 2016 to 2025

Organisations undertaking business in Ebola or Marburg affected areas should register with the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) returning workers scheme. Further disease-specific information is available for:

  • Ebola

  • Marburg

Ebola disease (EBOD) can be caused by Ebola (Zaire) virus (EVD), Sudan virus (SUDV), Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) or Tai Forest virus (TAFV). Marburg disease (MARD) is caused by Marburg virus.

Please note that this webpage will be updated on a weekly basis and therefore may not reflect the latest case numbers.

Current incidents and outbreaks

2026

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda

On  17 May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern for a new outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus affecting the DRC and Uganda. 

On 15 May 2026, DRC’s Ministry of Health (MoH) officially declared an Ebola outbreak affecting Ituri Province, eastern DRC, after sequencing at the National Institute for Biomedical Research Laboratory in Kinshasa confirmed the Bundibugyo strain. There is currently sustained community transmission in the DRC, with most cases reported from Ituri Province. For the latest case numbers please see the  DRC’s MoH situational reports.

Uganda’s MoH also declared a Bundibugyo virus outbreak on 15 May 2026, following laboratory confirmation in an individual with recent travel history to Ituri Province, DRC, who sought medical care at a hospital in Kampala. On 16 July 2026, Uganda began a 42-day countdown to declaring their outbreak over, after health authorities discharged the last recovered patient. A total of 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths have been reported in Uganda, of which 15 confirmed cases were imported from the DRC.

Figure 1. Cumulative number of confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease in affected countries

Please note that briefing maps are not to be taken as necessarily representing the views of the UK government on boundaries or political status. This map has been designed for briefing purposes only and should not be used to determine the precise location of places or features, or to serve as an authority on the delimitation of international boundaries or on the spelling of place and feature names. To note, 11 cases in Uganda have no district or city assigned and so are excluded.

Data sources: The World Bank, DRC MoH (health zone boundaries), Ebola DRC sitreps (22 August 2026), Ugandan Ministry of Health (25 August 2026).

As of 6 June 2026, WHO assesses the risk of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak as very high in the DRC, high for Uganda due to cross-border transmission through imported cases and ongoing epidemiological links to the DRC, high for countries with land borders adjoining countries with documented Bundibugyo virus detection, and low for the rest of the Africa Region.

The current risk of the outbreak to the UK population is assessed by UKHSA as low.

Uganda

On 30 June 2026, Uganda notified WHO of a confirmed case of Marburg disease in Kyegegwa District, which was identified through enhanced disease surveillance for Ebola.

Egyptian fruit bats (Rousettus aegyptiacus), the reservoir of Marburg virus, have historically been reported in Western Uganda in mining and cave environments. The last outbreak of Marburg disease in Uganda was reported in Kween district in October 2017.

Previous incidents and outbreaks: 2016 to 2025

2025

Ethiopia

On 12 November 2025, Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Ethiopian Public Health Institute reported an outbreak of suspected viral haemorrhagic fever in Jinka Town, South Ethiopia Regional State. On 14 November 2025 the Ethiopian MoH confirmed the outbreak to be caused by Marburg virus. Overall, the outbreak resulted in 14 confirmed cases, including 9 deaths and 5 recoveries. An additional 5 deaths of probable cases were reported. The outbreak was declared over on 26 January 2026.

This was the first outbreak of MARD to be reported in Ethiopia.

Democratic Republic of the Congo

On 4 September 2025, the DRC and WHO confirmed an outbreak of EBOD caused by Ebola (Zaire) virus. Overall, 64 cases (53 confirmed and 11 probable) including 45 deaths have been reported in Bulape Health Zone in Kasai province. The outbreak was declared over on 1 December 2025.

Genomic sequencing indicated that the outbreak was caused by a new zoonotic spillover, and was not linked to previous outbreaks in this region between 2007 and 2009. This was the 16th EBOD outbreak in the DRC since 1976. Previous outbreaks in Kasai province took place in 2007 and 2008.

Uganda

On 30 January 2025, Uganda’s MoH confirmed an outbreak of Sudan virus disease (SVD) in the capital, Kampala. Overall, 14 cases (12 confirmed and 2 probable cases, including 4 deaths) were reported from 7 districts and 3 cities: Kampala, Mbale District and City, Wakiso, Jinja District and City, Ntoroko, Fort Portal, and Kyegegwa. The outbreak was declared over on 26 April 2025.

This is the sixth outbreak of SVD to be reported in Uganda. The country last reported an outbreak of SVD in 2022.

United Republic of Tanzania

On 20 January 2025, WHO confirmed that an outbreak of MARD was occurring in Tanzania. Overall, 2 confirmed and 8 probable cases (all fatal) were reported, from Biharamulo district, Kagera region, Tanzania. The outbreak was declared over on 13 March 2025.

2024

Rwanda

On 27 September 2024, health authorities in Rwanda declared an outbreak of MARD. This was the first MARD outbreak to be reported in Rwanda and resulted in 66 confirmed cases including 15 deaths. Most cases were reported among healthcare workers in the capital, Kigali. The outbreak was declared over on 20 December 2024.

2023

Kagera region, United Republic of Tanzania

An outbreak of MARD was announced by Tanzania’s health authorities on 21 March 2023, in the north-western region of Kagera. This was the first ever outbreak of MARD to be reported in the country.

The outbreak had a total of 9 cases (8 confirmed and 1 probable), including 6 deaths, and was declared over on 2 June 2023.

Equatorial Guinea

On 13 February 2023, an outbreak of MARD was declared by Equatorial Guinean health authorities, after a case of MARD was confirmed in Kié Ntem Province, in the north-east of the country. This was the first ever outbreak of MARD to be reported in Equatorial Guinea. Four provinces (Centro Sur, Kie Ntem, Litoral and Wele-Nzas) were affected.

The outbreak, which had a total of 17 confirmed (including 12 deaths), and 23 probable cases (all fatal), was declared over on 8 June 2023.

2022

Uganda

An outbreak of SVD was declared by Uganda’s health authorities on 20 September 2022, after a case was confirmed in the Mubende District, Central Region.

This was the fifth outbreak of SVD to be reported in Uganda. The country last reported an outbreak of SVD in 2012.

The outbreak was declared over on 11 January 2023. In total, there were 164 cases (142 confirmed and 22 probable) and 77 deaths (55 confirmed and 22 probable). Cases were reported from 9 districts: Mubende, Kassanda, Kampala, Masaka and Wakiso in Central Region; Kyegegwa, Kagadi and Bunyangabu in Western Region; and Jinja in Eastern Region.

North Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)

On 21 August 2022, the Ministry of Health of the DRC announced that a new laboratory-confirmed case of EVD had been detected in the province of North Kivu. Genomic sequencing indicated that this case likely represented a new flare-up of the 2018 to 2020 North Kivu/Ituri EVD outbreak, initiated by transmission of Ebola virus from a persistently infected survivor, or a survivor who experienced a relapse.

This was the fourth EVD outbreak to be reported in the province since 2018.

The outbreak had a total of 1 confirmed case, which was fatal, and was declared over on 27 September 2022.

Ashanti region, Ghana

On 7 July 2022, Ghanaian health authorities announced the preliminary findings of 2 cases of MARD in the southern Ashanti region. An outbreak of MARD was subsequently declared on 17 July, following confirmatory testing of samples from one of the deceased cases, as performed by the Institut Pasteur in Dakar, Senegal.

The outbreak, which resulted in a total of 3 confirmed cases (a family cluster), including 2 deaths, was declared over on 16 September 2022.

Équateur Province, DRC

The DRC’s Ministry of Health announced a new laboratory confirmed case of EVD in Mbandaka City, Équateur Province on 23 April 2022. This was the third outbreak in the province since 2018.

Genome sequencing revealed that, whilst the new genome was closely related to those sequenced during the Équateur 2020 outbreak, it fell outside the 2020 outbreak clade, indicating that this case represents a new spill over event from a host reservoir and is not directly linked to the Équateur 2018 or Équateur 2020 EVD outbreaks.

The outbreak was declared over on 4 July 2022.

2021

North Kivu Province, DRC

On 8 October 2021, the DRC’s Ministry of Health announced that a new laboratory confirmed case of EVD had been detected in Butsili Health Area, Béni Health Zone in North Kivu Province. Earlier this year, an EVD outbreak in North Kivu Province was declared over on 3 May 2021.

The outbreak was declared over on 16 December 2021. During the outbreak, 8 confirmed (6 deaths) and 3 probable (3 deaths) cases were reported across 3 health areas (Butsili, Bundji and Kanzulinzuli) in the Béni Health Zone. More than 1,800 people were vaccinated in a campaign that launched just 5 days after the first case was detected.

Guéckédou Prefecture, Republic of Guinea

On 9 August 2021, an outbreak of MARD was declared in the Guéckédou Prefecture, South West Guinea, following laboratory confirmation of a single case. The outbreak occurred in the same N’zérékoré health region where 2 EVD outbreaks occurred in 2014 and 2021 (February to June 2021).

This was the first known case of MARD in Guinea and in West Africa. Only one case – the index patient who was diagnosed with the virus posthumously – was recorded during the outbreak, which was declared over on 15 September 2021.

Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the 2021 Guinean MARD was related to strains from the 2004 to 2005 MARD outbreak in Angola and to Marburg virus sequences obtained from bats in Sierra Leone during 2017 to 2018.

Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire

On 14 August 2021, Côte d’Ivoire’s Ministry of Health informed WHO of a suspected EVD case who was hospitalised in the commercial capital, Abidjan, after arriving from Guinea.

Following the announcement, and in line with WHO’s ‘no regrets’ policy, health authorities with support from WHO launched a public health response during which over 140 case contacts were followed up across the 2 countries. No contacts developed symptoms for the disease or tested positive for Ebola virus.

Re-confirmatory testing performed by the French National Reference Centre for Viral Haemorrhagic Fevers found no evidence of EVD in the original samples from the suspected case, and so the response was stood down on 31 August 2021.

N’zérékoré Prefecture, Republic of Guinea

On 14 February 2021, an outbreak of EVD was declared in Gouécké, in the prefecture of N’zérékoré, South East Guinea. Between 14 February and 19 June 2021, a total of 23 cases (16 confirmed and 7 probable) were identified in 4 sub-prefectures of N’zérékoré Prefecture. Of these confirmed and probable cases, 11 survived and 12 died. Five of the cases were health workers and one was a traditional health practitioner. A total of 10,873 people were vaccinated during the outbreak, including 885 case contacts and 2,779 front line workers.

This was Guinea’s second EVD outbreak, the first being the 2014 to 2016 West African EVD outbreak.

North Kivu Province, DRC

On 7 February 2021, DRC’s 12th EVD outbreak was declared in Butembo, a city in North Kivu Province in North East DRC. During the outbreak, there were 12 cases reported (11 confirmed), including 6 fatalities and 6 recoveries. The outbreak was declared over on 3 May 2021, just 3 months after the first case was reported, which was attributed to the prompt response of DRC’s health authorities and healthcare workers drawing upon their previous experiences in tackling outbreaks within the country.  

2020

Équateur Province, western DRC

Between 1 June and 18 November 2020, 130 EVD cases (119 confirmed and 11 probable), including 55 deaths, were reported from 13 of the 18 health zones in the province. This was DRC’s 11th EVD outbreak.

2018 to 2020

Eastern DRC

Between 1 August 2018 and 25 June 2020, 3,470 cases, 2,287 deaths and 1,171 survivors of EVD were reported across 3 provinces in DRC: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu. This outbreak, DRC’s 10th, is the longest lasting EVD incident in the country’s history, and the second-largest in the world after the 2014 to 2016 EVD outbreak in West Africa. The response to this outbreak was particularly challenging as it took place in an active conflict zone.

2019

United Republic of Tanzania

On 10 September 2019, WHO was made aware of unofficial reports of an unexplained death of a person in Dar es Salaam. It appears probable this was an Ebola-related death.

2018

Équateur Province, western DRC

Between 8 May and 24 July, 2018 DRC reported their ninth EVD outbreak which resulted in 54 cases (38 confirmed and 16 probable), including 33 deaths.

2017

Eastern Uganda

An outbreak of MARD in Kween district was confirmed on 17 October 2017. The 3 cases all died and WHO declared the outbreak over on 8 December 2017.

Bas-Uele Province, DRC

Between May and July 2017 an EVD outbreak consisting of 8 cases (5 confirmed), including 4 fatalities was recorded. This was DRC’s eighth EVD outbreak.

West Africa Ebola outbreak, 2014 to 2016

WHO confirmed an outbreak of EVD in south-eastern Guinea in March 2014. This was the first time an outbreak had been diagnosed in this part of Africa, and the index case was traced back to December 2013.

The outbreak spread to neighbouring and nearby countries, particularly Liberia and Sierra Leone, and became the largest ever known outbreak of this disease. It continued for more than 2 years and a total of 28,616 confirmed, probable and suspected cases were reported in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, with 11,310 deaths.

See final WHO Ebola situation report, June 2016.

Linked Ebola outbreaks and cases in other countries (2014 to 2015)

Mali

Two importations leading to a total of 8 cases.

Nigeria

Twenty cases in Lagos and Port Harcourt, following an initial importation from Liberia.

Senegal

A single case imported from Guinea.

Italy

One case in a returning healthcare worker.

Spain

One case in a healthcare worker involved in the care of patients repatriated from West Africa.

United Kingdom

One case was imported into Scotland in December 2014. The patient was a healthcare worker who had been working in an Ebola treatment centre in Sierra Leone.

United States

A single EVD case was imported from Liberia into Texas in September 2014. Transmission to 2 healthcare workers subsequently occurred. A further case of EVD was confirmed in a humanitarian aid worker who returned from Guinea in October 2014.

You can find more information on EBOD outbreaks prior to 2014.
